MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 5
   C. 7
   D. 8

2. Round 553 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 540
   B. 500
   C. 560
   D. 550

3. Which number is written in words as "two thousand and ninety"? (1 mark)
   A. 290
   B. 20,900
   C. 2,090
   D. 2,900

4. In the number 91,724, the digit 9 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Ten thousands
   C. Ones
   D. Hundreds

5. What is the smallest 5-digit number? (1 mark)
   A. 99,999
   B. 9,999
   C. 1,000
   D. 10,000

6. A shop sold 3,275 kg of maize in May and 4,860 kg in June. How many kilograms did it sell altogether? (1 mark)
   A. 8,125 kg
   B. 8,235 kg
   C. 8,135 kg
   D. 7,035 kg

7. Work out 6,003 − 2,475. (1 mark)
   A. 3,428
   B. 4,472
   C. 3,538
   D. 3,528

8. Which sum checks that 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528? (1 mark)
   A. 3,528 + 2,475
   B. 6,003 + 3,528
   C. 3,528 − 2,475
   D. 6,003 + 2,475

9. Estimate 5,064 − 1,927 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 3,230
   B. 3,130
   C. 3,120
   D. 3,140

10. Work out 5,432 − 2,718. (1 mark)
   A. 3,326
   B. 2,614
   C. 2,714
   D. 2,724

11. What is 15 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 600
   B. 60
   C. 55
   D. 6,000

12. Which pattern has the rule multiply by 2? (1 mark)
   A. 5, 10, 15, 20
   B. 3, 5, 7, 9
   C. 2, 4, 8, 16
   D. 2, 4, 6, 8

13. What is 60 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 600
   B. 60,000
   C. 160
   D. 6,000

14. Change 31/10 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/10
   B. 1 3/10
   C. 3 1/10
   D. 4 1/10

15. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/12
   B. 12/5
   C. 5/7
   D. 5/12

16. A circle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/10
   B. 3/10
   C. 3/7
   D. 10/3

17. Dan writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 3/8
   B. 8/3
   C. 4 2/3
   D. 1/2

18. Change 1 5/6 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 11/6
   B. 6/6
   C. 12/6
   D. 11/7

19. In the number 9.27, the digit 7 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Tenths
   C. Ones
   D. Hundredths

20. Write 6/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.06
   B. 6.0
   C. 0.006
   D. 0.6

21. What is 8 m − 3 m 40 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 50 cm
   B. 4 m 70 cm
   C. 4 m 60 cm
   D. 5 m 60 cm

22. Which sum finds the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns? (1 mark)
   A. 4 × 6
   B. 4 + 6
   C. 4 − 6
   D. 6 ÷ 4

23. A tile is 10 cm long and 10 cm wide. It is covered with 1 cm squares. How many squares fit? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 40
   C. 100
   D. 10

24. Why should heavy boxes be stacked at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. So that the boxes are hidden
   B. So that the volume increases
   C. It makes no difference
   D. So that the stack is stable and does not fall

25. What is 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 4 3/4 kg
   C. 4 1/2 kg
   D. 5 1/4 kg

26. What is 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 4 3/4 kg
   C. 4 1/2 kg
   D. 5 1/4 kg

27. What is 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 1 kg
   B. 1 3/4 kg
   C. 1 1/4 kg
   D. 1 1/2 kg

28. Change 135 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 15 min
   B. 3 h 15 min
   C. 2 h 45 min
   D. 1 h 45 min

29. Change 72 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 6 days
   B. 4 days
   C. 1.2 days
   D. 3 days

30. What is 7 h 15 min − 3 h 50 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 15 min
   B. 4 h 25 min
   C. 3 h 25 min
   D. 3 h 35 min

31. One unit costs Ksh 65. What is the cost of 3 exercise books? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 195
   B. Ksh 130
   C. Ksh 68
   D. Ksh 205

32. A customer pays with Ksh 1,000 for goods that cost Ksh 750. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 250
   B. Ksh 350
   C. Ksh 1,750
   D. Ksh 240

33. A customer pays with Ksh 200 for goods that cost Ksh 145. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 45
   B. Ksh 55
   C. Ksh 155
   D. Ksh 345

34. Two quarter turns together make (1 mark)
   A. a full turn
   B. a three-quarter turn
   C. a quarter turn
   D. a half turn

35. Which shape has three straight sides? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle
   B. Triangle
   C. Square
   D. Circle

36. Which is a good tool for drawing straight lines in a table? (1 mark)
   A. A measuring jug
   B. A clock
   C. A beam balance
   D. A ruler

37. In a tally chart, 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 9
   C. 5
   D. 3

38. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are mango or pawpaw together? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 6
   C. 4
   D. 7

39. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 9
   C. 11
   D. 10

40. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. How many are blue or green together? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 7
   C. 6
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A learner writes 5 in the mango row but the tally shows 4. Explain why this is a mistake and how to avoid it. (3 marks)

42. A shop buys 24 boxes of pencils. Each box has 36 pencils. (a) Estimate the number of pencils by rounding to the nearest ten. (b) Work out the exact number of pencils. (5 marks)

43. A trader has 25 kg of rice. She sells 7 1/2 kg to one customer and 6 3/4 kg to another. How much rice does she have left? (5 marks)

44. Express 23/6 as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

45. Tabitha has 2,450 eggs. She gets 3,875 more. How many eggs does she have now? (3 marks)

46. Mama Kioko sells 3 bags of mangoes (m) and 2 bags of oranges (o) on Monday, then 1 bag of mangoes and 4 bags of oranges on Tuesday. Write an expression and simplify it. (4 marks)

47. A hundred square has 60 of its small squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal. (2 marks)

48. Work out 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L. (3 marks)

49. A school uniform costs a shirt Ksh 650, shorts Ksh 800 and shoes Ksh 1,900. Find the total cost and the change from Ksh 5,000. (4 marks)

50. Fill in the 3 times table from 3 × 1 to 3 × 10. Describe one pattern you notice. (4 marks)

51. Describe how to make a 1/2 kg mass from sand using a 1 kg mass and a beam balance. (4 marks)

52. Wanjiku has 2 L of milk and buys 1 1/2 L more. How much milk does she have now? (2 marks)

53. Add 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

54. The floor of a shop has 8 rows of 12 square tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (3 marks)

55. School starts at 8:00 a.m. and ends at 3:15 p.m. Lunch is from 12:40 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. (a) How long is the school day? (b) How long is it from the start of school to the start of lunch? (c) How long is it from the end of lunch to the end of school? (5 marks)

56. Explain how a quarter turn is related to a right angle and how four quarter turns are related to a full turn. (3 marks)

57. How many right angles does a rectangle have? Explain. (2 marks)

58. A bag has a mass of 5 kg. Musa takes out 1 1/2 kg of beans. What mass is left in the bag? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 9
   36 ÷ 9 = 4 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 36. The others leave a remainder.

2. D — 550
   Look at the ones digit 3. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 553 rounds to 550.

3. C — 2,090
   two thousand and ninety: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 2,090.

4. B — Ten thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 9 is in the ten thousands place.

5. D — 10,000
   Adding 1 to 9,999 gives 10,000, the smallest number with five digits.

6. C — 8,135 kg
   Add 3,275 + 4,860 = 8,135 kg.

7. D — 3,528
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.

8. A — 3,528 + 2,475
   Addition undoes subtraction. 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003, the starting number.

9. B — 3,130
   5,064 rounds to 5,060 and 1,927 rounds to 1,930. 5,060 − 1,930 = 3,130.

10. C — 2,714
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714. Check: 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432.

11. A — 600
   15 × 4 = 60, then × 10 gives 600.

12. C — 2, 4, 8, 16
   2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. The other patterns add 2 or add 5.

13. D — 6,000
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 60 × 100 = 6,000.

14. C — 3 1/10
   31 ÷ 10 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/10, so 31/10 = 3 1/10.

15. D — 5/12
   The whole has 12 equal parts and 5 are shaded, so 5/12 is shaded.

16. B — 3/10
   Not shaded: 10 − 7 = 3 parts, so 3/10.

17. B — 8/3
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 8/3 is one whole or more.

18. A — 11/6
   1 × 6 = 6 and 6 + 5 = 11. The denominator stays 6, so the answer is 11/6.

19. D — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 9.27 the digit 7 is in the hundredths place.

20. A — 0.06
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 6/100 = 0.06.

21. C — 4 m 60 cm
   800 − 340 = 460 cm = 4 m 60 cm.

22. A — 4 × 6
   Area is the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

23. C — 100
   10 rows × 10 columns = 100 squares.

24. D — So that the stack is stable and does not fall
   A stack with heavy boxes at the bottom is more stable and safer.

25. B — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

26. B — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

27. C — 1 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 kg − 1 3/4 kg = 1 1/4 kg.

28. A — 2 h 15 min
   135 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 15, so 135 minutes = 2 h 15 min.

29. D — 3 days
   72 ÷ 24 = 3 days.

30. C — 3 h 25 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 25 min.

31. A — Ksh 195
   Cost = number × price = 3 × 65 = Ksh 195.

32. A — Ksh 250
   Change = amount paid − cost = 1,000 − 750 = Ksh 250.

33. B — Ksh 55
   Change = amount paid − cost = 200 − 145 = Ksh 55.

34. D — a half turn
   1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, so two quarter turns make a half turn.

35. B — Triangle
   A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.

36. D — A ruler
   A ruler is used to draw straight lines.

37. A — 4
   0 × 5 + 4 = 4.

38. A — 5
   4 + 1 = 5.

39. D — 10
   Add all the numbers: 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10.

40. C — 6
   4 + 2 = 6.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The number in the table must match the tally, otherwise the total will not add up correctly. Count the tallies carefully and check the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mismatch, 1 mark for the effect on total, 1 mark for checking.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 20 × 40 = 800 (b) 864 pencils
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 800, 2 marks for 36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720, 1 mark for 864.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: 10 3/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Total sold: 7 1/2 + 6 3/4 = 7 2/4 + 6 3/4 = 13 5/4 = 14 1/4 kg (3 marks). 25 − 14 1/4 = 10 3/4 kg (2 marks).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 5/6
   Working / marking points: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (2 marks). Write 3 5/6 with the same denominator (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6,325 eggs
   Working / marking points: Ones 0 + 5 = 5; tens 5 + 7 = 12 write 2 carry 1; hundreds 4 + 8 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1; thousands 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. 1 mark for method, 1 for regrouping, 1 for answer with unit.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the expression, 1 mark for 4m, 1 mark for 6o, 1 mark for the final answer.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60/100 and 0.6 (or 0.60)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the fraction and 1 mark for the decimal.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); answer 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 3,350; change Ksh 1,650
   Working / marking points: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350 (2 marks); 5,000 − 3,350 = 1,650 (2 marks).

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. Each product is 3 more than the one before it (or the products alternate odd and even).
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the table (1 mark if one or two errors), 2 marks for a correct pattern with a reason.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Balance a bag of sand against the 1 kg mass. Share the sand equally into two bags, checking with the balance that they are level. Each bag is 1/2 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balancing sand with 1 kg, 1 mark for sharing into two bags, 1 mark for checking they balance, 1 mark for stating each is 1/2 kg.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 2 + 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the addition and 1 mark for the unit.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 m 25 cm
   Working / marking points: 345 + 280 = 625 cm (2 marks); 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm (1 mark).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 96 tiles
   Working / marking points: 8 × 12 (1 mark); 80 + 16 (1 mark); 96 tiles (1 mark).

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 7 hours 15 minutes (b) 4 hours 40 minutes (c) 1 hour 35 minutes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 7 hours and then 15 minutes (2 marks); (b) 8:00 to 12:40 is 4 h 40 min (1 mark); (c) 1:40 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 1 h 35 min (2 marks).

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quarter turn makes a right angle. Four quarter turns, that is four right angles, make a full turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for quarter turn = right angle, 1 mark for four quarters, 1 mark for full turn.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4. A rectangle has four corners and each corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 and 1 mark for the reason.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 5 − 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.
